eligibility_note: Exposure criterion met as ICT in general: the only estimated exposure is the Digital Evolution Index (composite of digital supply, demand, institutions, innovation; text: 'DEI will be used as a proxy of digital transformation'). It is not an AI measure; AI appears only in title, abstract framing and policy discussion, so stream H (general ICT/digital), not AI, is right and the 3-economy AI rule does not apply. 25 economies >= 10; own OLS/FGLS estimation; outcomes labour productivity, GNI per capita and employment qualify. Caveat: eligibility rests on a broad digital composite that also loads on institutions and innovation.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: single 2017 cross-section, 3-4 controls, no instrument or lag, richer countries score higher on digital indices, yet text says 'digital transformation increases productivity'.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: too_harsh: a composite digital index, while overlapping with institutions and income, does capture general ICT/digital evolution, and the AI mismatch is a framing issue, not a measurement failure for the ICT-in-general claim; moderate fits better.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: 25 author-chosen developing countries spanning Digital Planet zones, one year, N too small for the controls used.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: WDI productivity and GNI per capita are standard; ILO modelled employment and 'most recent figure' labour cost add noise.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: non-standard FGLS (weights added as a regressor), N=25 with up to 4 regressors, no robustness checks, equations with differing controls; index chosen partly for higher R-squared.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: all four equations and gender splits reported, but no robustness or alternative indices in regressions; moderate is fair.
risk_of_bias.why: Serious overall is right because causal-sounding conclusions rest on a tiny cross-section with no strategy for reverse causation; the exposure domain alone could be moderate.

problems: No invented numbers or paper mix-ups found. Minor: record says >100 indicators vs '170 indicator' in text; Table 2 reports no N/R-squared (N=25 inferred); signs are lost in the converted table so directions rely on the authors' text; Table 2 note's star scheme ('90, 95 and 99%') is inconsistent with the Weights row stars (as the record noted); OLS is not significant for employment, so the positive employment finding holds only under FGLS.
